RenderSettings._: Settings that decide how big, how fast, and in what style your final picture or movie is made and saved.
RenderSettings.resolution_x: How many pixels wide the image is. Low is small and quick to render; high is sharp but slower.
RenderSettings.resolution_y: How many pixels tall the image is. Low is small and quick to render; high is sharp but slower.
RenderSettings.resolution_percentage: Shrinks or grows the render without changing X and Y. 50% is a fast draft, 100% is full size.
RenderSettings.preview_pixel_size: Makes the viewport preview chunkier so it is faster. Bigger blocks are quicker but blurrier.
RenderSettings.preview_pixel_size.AUTO: Blender picks the pixel size to match your screen's UI scale.
RenderSettings.preview_pixel_size.1: Every pixel is drawn. Sharpest preview, slowest.
RenderSettings.preview_pixel_size.2: Draws in 2x2 blocks. Half the detail, much faster.
RenderSettings.preview_pixel_size.4: Draws in 4x4 blocks. Blurry but very fast.
RenderSettings.preview_pixel_size.8: Draws in 8x8 blocks. Very chunky, fastest preview.
RenderSettings.pixel_aspect_x: Makes pixels wider or narrower. Leave at 1 unless you need stretched (anamorphic) video.
RenderSettings.pixel_aspect_y: Makes pixels taller or shorter. Leave at 1 unless you need stretched (anamorphic) video.
RenderSettings.ppm_factor: Print density saved inside the image file (pixels per unit). Only matters if you print the image.
RenderSettings.ppm_base: The unit used for print density, such as meters or inches. Works with PPM Factor.
RenderSettings.fps: Frames per second: how many pictures make one second of movie. 24 is film, 30 is TV, higher is smoother.
RenderSettings.fps_base: A small divider for FPS to get odd speeds like 29.97. Leave at 1 normally.
RenderSettings.frame_map_old: The old length of the animation to stretch or squash. Use with New to slow down or speed up the render.
RenderSettings.frame_map_new: The new length that the Old frames will fill. Bigger than Old means slow motion.
RenderSettings.dither_intensity: Adds tiny noise to hide color banding in smooth gradients. 0 is off; higher is noisier but smoother.
RenderSettings.filter_size: How much neighbor pixels blend to smooth edges. Low is sharp and jagged; high is soft and blurry.
RenderSettings.film_transparent: Hides the world background so the render has see-through areas. Great for putting it over another picture.
RenderSettings.use_freestyle: Turns on Freestyle, which draws cartoon-like outlines on your models.
RenderSettings.threads: How many CPU cores the render may use. More cores render faster but use more of your computer.
RenderSettings.threads_mode: Choose if Blender picks the number of CPU cores or you set it yourself.
RenderSettings.threads_mode.AUTO: Blender uses all the cores it finds on your computer.
RenderSettings.threads_mode.FIXED: You choose exactly how many cores to use with the Threads number.
RenderSettings.use_motion_blur: Smears fast-moving things like a real camera does. Makes movement look more natural.
RenderSettings.motion_blur_shutter: How long the virtual shutter stays open. Low is a tiny blur; high is a long streaky blur.
RenderSettings.motion_blur_position: Chooses when the blur happens relative to the frame: before it, around it, or after it.
RenderSettings.motion_blur_position.START: The blur trails ahead of the frame's moment, showing where things go next.
RenderSettings.motion_blur_position.CENTER: The blur is spread evenly before and after the frame. Most natural.
RenderSettings.motion_blur_position.END: The blur trails behind the frame's moment, showing where things came from.
RenderSettings.hair_type: The shape used to draw hair and curves in renders. Simpler shapes render faster.
RenderSettings.hair_type.STRAND: Draws each hair as a thin line. Fast, good for fine hair.
RenderSettings.hair_type.STRIP: Draws each hair as a flat ribbon. Good for medium thickness.
RenderSettings.hair_type.CYLINDER: Draws each hair as a round tube. Best-looking up close, slowest.
RenderSettings.hair_subdiv: Adds extra smoothing steps along curves. 0 is angular; higher is smoother but heavier.
RenderSettings.use_high_quality_normals: Makes shading on curved surfaces more accurate. Looks better but can be a little slower.
RenderSettings.anisotropic_filter: Keeps textures sharp when seen at a steep angle, like a floor far away. Higher is sharper but slower.
RenderSettings.anisotropic_filter.FILTER_0: Off. Textures blur at steep angles. Fastest.
RenderSettings.anisotropic_filter.FILTER_16: Maximum sharpness at steep angles. Slowest.
RenderSettings.use_border: Only renders a rectangle you draw (Shift+B in the camera view). Saves time when testing one area.
RenderSettings.border_min_x: Left edge of the render region, from 0 (far left) to 1 (far right).
RenderSettings.border_min_y: Bottom edge of the render region, from 0 (bottom) to 1 (top).
RenderSettings.border_max_x: Right edge of the render region, from 0 (far left) to 1 (far right).
RenderSettings.border_max_y: Top edge of the render region, from 0 (bottom) to 1 (top).
RenderSettings.use_crop_to_border: Cuts the final image down to just the render region instead of keeping the empty rest.
RenderSettings.use_placeholder: Creates an empty file for each frame at the start. Lets several computers share the work without clashing.
RenderSettings.use_overwrite: When on, new frames replace old files. When off, frames that already exist are skipped.
RenderSettings.save_output: Saves each rendered frame of an animation to your disk. Turn off to only watch the render.
RenderSettings.use_compositing: Runs your render through the compositor node setup (color tweaks, glows, etc.) if you made one.
RenderSettings.use_sequencer: Sends the render through the Video Sequencer so edited strips are included in the final result.
RenderSettings.use_file_extension: Adds the ending like .png or .mp4 to the file name automatically.
RenderSettings.use_lock_interface: Freezes the Blender window while rendering to give the render more memory.
RenderSettings.filepath: Where animation frames or videos are saved. Use # symbols for frame numbers, like frame_####.
RenderSettings.use_render_cache: Saves partial render results to disk so heavy compositing does not have to redo them.
RenderSettings.use_stamp_time: Writes the frame's time (hours:minutes:seconds:frames) into the image information.
RenderSettings.use_stamp_date: Writes today's date and time into the image information.
RenderSettings.use_stamp_frame: Writes the frame number into the image information.
RenderSettings.use_stamp_frame_range: Writes the start and end frames of the animation into the image information.
RenderSettings.use_stamp_camera: Writes the name of the active camera into the image information.
RenderSettings.use_stamp_lens: Writes the camera's lens size (focal length) into the image information.
RenderSettings.use_stamp_scene: Writes the scene's name into the image information.
RenderSettings.use_stamp_note: Adds your own note text to the image information.
RenderSettings.use_stamp_marker: Writes the name of the most recent timeline marker into the image information.
RenderSettings.use_stamp_filename: Writes the name of your .blend file into the image information.
RenderSettings.use_stamp_sequencer_strip: Writes the name of the top video strip in the sequencer into the image information.
RenderSettings.use_stamp_render_time: Writes how long the render took into the image information.
RenderSettings.stamp_note_text: The text of your own note to show in the stamp when Note is on.
RenderSettings.use_stamp: Prints the stamp info as visible words on the image itself, like a label in the corner.
RenderSettings.use_stamp_labels: Shows names like 'Camera:' in front of each value in the stamp. Off shows only the values.
RenderSettings.metadata_input: Chooses whether stamp info comes from the scene or from the video strips being edited.
RenderSettings.metadata_input.SCENE: Uses the current scene's own information.
RenderSettings.metadata_input.STRIPS: Uses the information stored in each video strip in the sequencer.
RenderSettings.use_stamp_memory: Writes the most computer memory used during the render into the image information.
RenderSettings.use_stamp_hostname: Writes the name of the computer that made the render into the image information.
RenderSettings.stamp_font_size: How big the stamp text is. Bigger numbers make larger letters.
RenderSettings.stamp_foreground: The color of the stamp text.
RenderSettings.stamp_background: The color of the box behind the stamp text, so it is easy to read.
RenderSettings.sequencer_gl_preview: How 3D scenes look inside the video sequencer's preview. Simpler styles are faster.
RenderSettings.sequencer_gl_preview.WIREFRAME: Shows only the outlines of objects. Fastest.
RenderSettings.sequencer_gl_preview.SOLID: Shows plain solid shapes with simple lighting.
RenderSettings.sequencer_gl_preview.MATERIAL: Shows objects with their materials and basic lighting.
RenderSettings.sequencer_gl_preview.RENDERED: Shows the full rendered look. Prettiest, slowest.
RenderSettings.use_sequencer_override_scene_strip: Uses the sequencer scene's own Workbench and world settings instead of each strip's scene.
RenderSettings.use_single_layer: Renders only the layer you are working on, instead of all layers. Handy for quick tests.
RenderSettings.use_multiview: Turns on multiple camera views at once, used for 3D stereo (left eye and right eye) output.
RenderSettings.views_format: Chooses how multiple views are set up: simple left/right 3D, or a custom list of views.
RenderSettings.views_format.STEREO_3D: Two views, left eye and right eye, for 3D glasses or VR.
RenderSettings.views_format.MULTIVIEW: Any number of custom camera views you define yourself.
RenderSettings.engine: Which render engine draws your picture. Different engines trade speed against realism.
RenderSettings.engine.BLENDER_EEVEE: EEVEE, Blender's fast engine. Looks great and renders quickly using your graphics card.
RenderSettings.use_simplify: Turns on shortcuts that make the scene lighter and faster, at the cost of detail.
RenderSettings.simplify_subdivision: Caps how smooth (subdivided) models can be in the viewport. Low is faster but blockier.
RenderSettings.simplify_child_particles: Shows only this percentage of child particles (like hair strands) in the viewport. Low is faster.
RenderSettings.simplify_subdivision_render: Caps how smooth (subdivided) models can be in the final render. Low is faster but blockier.
RenderSettings.simplify_child_particles_render: Uses only this percentage of child particles (like hair strands) in the final render.
RenderSettings.simplify_volumes: Lowers the detail of smoke and fog shapes in the viewport. Low is faster but blurrier.
RenderSettings.use_simplify_normals: Skips fancy smooth-shading data in the viewport so heavy models display faster.
RenderSettings.use_texture_cache: Loads image textures in small pieces at the size needed. Saves memory in scenes with huge textures.
RenderSettings.use_auto_generate_texture_cache: Makes the special cache files (.tx) for your textures automatically when rendering if missing.
RenderSettings.simplify_gpencil: Turns on speed-saving shortcuts for Grease Pencil 2D drawings.
RenderSettings.simplify_gpencil_onplay: Applies the Grease Pencil shortcuts only while the animation is playing.
RenderSettings.simplify_gpencil_antialiasing: Smooths jagged edges of Grease Pencil lines. Off is faster but rougher.
RenderSettings.simplify_gpencil_view_fill: Shows the colored fill inside Grease Pencil shapes. Off hides fills for speed.
RenderSettings.simplify_gpencil_modifier: Shows Grease Pencil modifiers. Off ignores them for speed.
RenderSettings.simplify_gpencil_shader_fx: Shows Grease Pencil visual effects like blur or glow. Off ignores them for speed.
RenderSettings.simplify_gpencil_tint: Shows the color tint of Grease Pencil layers. Off ignores tints.
RenderSettings.use_persistent_data: Keeps scene data in memory between renders so re-renders start faster. Uses more memory.
RenderSettings.line_thickness_mode: Chooses how Freestyle outline thickness is measured.
RenderSettings.line_thickness_mode.ABSOLUTE: Lines are a fixed number of pixels thick, no matter the image size.
RenderSettings.line_thickness_mode.RELATIVE: Lines scale with the image size, so they keep the same look when resized.
RenderSettings.line_thickness: How thick Freestyle outlines are, in pixels. Low is thin lines; high is bold lines.
RenderSettings.compositor_device: Chooses whether compositor effects are calculated by the CPU or the graphics card.
RenderSettings.compositor_device.CPU: Uses the processor. Works everywhere, usually slower.
RenderSettings.compositor_device.GPU: Uses the graphics card. Usually much faster.
RenderSettings.compositor_precision: How exact the compositor's math is. Higher is more accurate but uses more memory.
RenderSettings.compositor_precision.AUTO: Blender picks the precision based on what the nodes need.
RenderSettings.compositor_precision.FULL: Always uses full precision. Most accurate, uses the most memory.
RenderSettings.compositor_denoise_device: Which part of your computer cleans noise in the compositor's Denoise nodes.
RenderSettings.compositor_denoise_device.AUTO: Blender picks the best device for you.
RenderSettings.compositor_denoise_device.GPU: The graphics card does the denoising. Usually faster.
RenderSettings.compositor_denoise_preview_quality: How carefully noise is cleaned while previewing. Higher looks cleaner but is slower.
RenderSettings.compositor_denoise_preview_quality.BALAN: A middle choice between speed and quality.
RenderSettings.compositor_denoise_preview_quality.FAST: Quickest, but may leave some noise.
RenderSettings.compositor_denoise_final_quality: How carefully noise is cleaned in the final render. Higher looks cleaner but is slower.
RenderSettings.compositor_denoise_final_quality.BALANCE: A middle choice between speed and quality.
RenderSettings.compositor_denoise_final_quality.FAST: Quickest, but may leave some noise.

ImageFormatSettings._: Settings for what kind of file your render is saved as, and how much quality and color detail it keeps.
ImageFormatSettings.media_type: Whether you save a single picture, a picture with several layers, or a video.
ImageFormatSettings.media_type.IMAGE: A normal single picture file such as PNG or JPEG.
ImageFormatSettings.media_type.MULTI_LAYER_IMAGE: One file holding several layers and passes, so you can edit them separately later.
ImageFormatSettings.media_type.VIDEO: A movie file made from all the rendered frames.
ImageFormatSettings.file_format: The type of file the render is saved as. It decides quality, size and what the file can store.
ImageFormatSettings.file_format.AVIF: Modern compact image with good quality at small size. Not supported by every program yet.
ImageFormatSettings.file_format.JPEG: Small file, but lossy and no transparency. Good for sharing photos online.
ImageFormatSettings.file_format.OPEN_EXR: Professional format that keeps extra brightness range. Best for editing the render later.
ImageFormatSettings.file_format.PNG: Lossless picture with transparency support. A safe everyday choice.
ImageFormatSettings.file_format.WEBP: Web-friendly image that is small and can have transparency.
ImageFormatSettings.file_format.BMP: Old, uncompressed image. Big files, rarely needed.
ImageFormatSettings.file_format.CINEON: Film-industry image format using logarithmic color. Used in movie pipelines.
ImageFormatSettings.file_format.DPX: Film and video industry image format. Common in professional movie work.
ImageFormatSettings.file_format.IRIS: Very old image format from Silicon Graphics computers. Rarely used today.
ImageFormatSettings.file_format.JPEG2000: Newer JPEG with better quality per size. Used in cinema and archives.
ImageFormatSettings.file_format.HDR: Radiance HDR image that keeps extra brightness range but no transparency.
ImageFormatSettings.file_format.TARGA: Older game-industry image with transparency, lightly compressed.
ImageFormatSettings.file_format.TARGA_RAW: Targa image with no compression. Bigger files but simple.
ImageFormatSettings.file_format.TIFF: High-quality image often used in printing and photography.
ImageFormatSettings.file_format.OPEN_EXR_MULTILAYER: EXR file that stores every render layer and pass in one file.
ImageFormatSettings.file_format.FFMPEG: Saves a video file instead of separate pictures, using the FFmpeg settings.
ImageFormatSettings.color_mode: Which color channels are saved: grayscale, color, or color plus transparency.
ImageFormatSettings.color_mode.BW: Black and white only. Smallest file.
ImageFormatSettings.color_mode.RGB: Full color (red, green, blue) with no transparency.
ImageFormatSettings.color_mode.RGBA: Full color plus an alpha channel for see-through areas.
ImageFormatSettings.color_depth: How many bits store each color channel. More bits give smoother gradients and bigger files.
ImageFormatSettings.color_depth.8: Standard quality, good for normal viewing and web.
ImageFormatSettings.color_depth.10: More shades per color. Used in some video workflows.
ImageFormatSettings.color_depth.12: Even more shades, used in cinema formats.
ImageFormatSettings.color_depth.16: Very smooth gradients, good for editing later.
ImageFormatSettings.color_depth.32: Highest precision, full float. Large files, used with EXR.
ImageFormatSettings.quality: How much detail lossy formats like JPEG keep. Low makes small, blocky files; high looks cleaner.
ImageFormatSettings.compression: How hard the file is squeezed. 0 is fast and big; 100 is slow and small. Quality is not lost.
ImageFormatSettings.use_preview: When rendering an animation, also saves small JPEG preview pictures in the same folder.
ImageFormatSettings.exr_codec: The method used to compress an EXR file. It trades file size, speed and quality.
ImageFormatSettings.exr_codec.NONE: No compression. Largest files, fastest to save.
ImageFormatSettings.exr_codec.ZIP: Lossless compression that works on groups of lines. A solid all-round choice.
ImageFormatSettings.exr_codec.PIZ: Lossless compression that works well on noisy or grainy images.
ImageFormatSettings.exr_codec.DWAA: Lossy compression with small files. Good for final images.
ImageFormatSettings.exr_codec.DWAB: Lossy like DWAA but works on bigger blocks, so it reads faster.
ImageFormatSettings.exr_codec.HTJ2K: Modern fast compression based on JPEG 2000. Needs newer software to open.
ImageFormatSettings.exr_codec.ZIPS: Lossless compression done one line at a time. Slightly bigger than ZIP.
ImageFormatSettings.exr_codec.RLE: Simple lossless compression. Fast, best for flat areas of color.
ImageFormatSettings.exr_codec.PXR24: Lossless for most data but trims 32-bit precision. Good for depth passes.
ImageFormatSettings.exr_codec.B44: Lossy, fixed ratio, quick to read. Handy for real-time playback.
ImageFormatSettings.exr_codec.B44A: Like B44 but does better on flat areas such as alpha channels.
ImageFormatSettings.use_exr_interleave: Stores EXR layers in an older mixed-together layout so older programs can open the file.
ImageFormatSettings.use_jpeg2k_ycc: Saves brightness and color separately instead of red, green, blue. Makes smaller files.
ImageFormatSettings.use_jpeg2k_cinema_preset: Uses settings that meet the digital cinema standard.
ImageFormatSettings.use_jpeg2k_cinema_48: Uses the digital cinema settings made for 48 frames per second.
ImageFormatSettings.jpeg2k_codec: The file wrapper used for JPEG 2000.
ImageFormatSettings.jpeg2k_codec.JP2: Standard .jp2 file with extra info stored inside.
ImageFormatSettings.jpeg2k_codec.J2K: Bare .j2k data stream without the extra wrapper.
ImageFormatSettings.tiff_codec: How the TIFF file is compressed.
ImageFormatSettings.tiff_codec.NONE: No compression. Biggest files, opens everywhere.
ImageFormatSettings.tiff_codec.DEFLATE: Lossless compression that gives small files. Widely supported.
ImageFormatSettings.tiff_codec.LZW: Older lossless compression that most programs understand.
ImageFormatSettings.tiff_codec.PACKBITS: Very simple lossless compression. Fast but not very small.
ImageFormatSettings.use_cineon_log: Converts colors to a logarithmic scale, the way film scans store them.
ImageFormatSettings.cineon_black: The log value that counts as pure black when converting. Lower values reveal darker detail.
ImageFormatSettings.cineon_white: The log value that counts as pure white when converting. Higher values keep more highlights.
ImageFormatSettings.cineon_gamma: Adjusts mid-tone brightness during log conversion. Higher makes mid-tones darker.
ImageFormatSettings.views_format: How stereo or multi-camera views are saved: separate files or combined.
ImageFormatSettings.views_format.INDIVIDUAL: Each view is saved as its own file.
ImageFormatSettings.views_format.STEREO_3D: Left and right eye views are combined into one 3D image.
ImageFormatSettings.views_format.MULTIVIEW: All views are stored together in one multi-view file.
ImageFormatSettings.color_management: Chooses whether the saved file uses the scene's color settings or its own.
ImageFormatSettings.color_management.FOLLOW_SCENE: Uses the scene's View Transform, Look, and other color settings.
ImageFormatSettings.color_management.OVERRIDE: Lets this output use its own color settings instead.

FFmpegSettings._: Settings for making a video file: container, codec, quality, file size, and audio.
FFmpegSettings.format: The container is the video file type, like .mp4 or .mkv. It holds the video and audio together.
FFmpegSettings.format.MPEG4: MP4, the most common format. Plays almost everywhere.
FFmpegSettings.format.MKV: Matroska, a flexible container that can hold many kinds of video and audio.
FFmpegSettings.format.WEBM: A web-friendly format made for browsers.
FFmpegSettings.format.AVI: An old Windows format. Large files, widely understood.
FFmpegSettings.format.DV: Digital video format used by old tape camcorders.
FFmpegSettings.format.FLASH: Old Flash video format. Mostly obsolete.
FFmpegSettings.format.MPEG2: Format used for DVDs and older broadcast TV.
FFmpegSettings.format.OGG: Open, free container, mostly used for audio.
FFmpegSettings.format.QUICKTIME: Apple's .mov format, popular in video editing.
FFmpegSettings.codec: The codec is the method that compresses video frames. It decides quality, file size and compatibility.
FFmpegSettings.codec.NONE: No video is saved. Use if you only want audio.
FFmpegSettings.codec.AV1: Very efficient modern codec. Small files but slow to encode.
FFmpegSettings.codec.H264: Most popular codec. Good quality, small files, plays nearly everywhere.
FFmpegSettings.codec.H265: Newer than H.264. Smaller files for the same quality, but not on every device.
FFmpegSettings.codec.WEBM: VP9 codec for WebM files, made for web video.
FFmpegSettings.codec.DNXHD: Professional editing codec by Avid. Big, high-quality files.
FFmpegSettings.codec.DV: Codec used by old digital camcorders.
FFmpegSettings.codec.FFV1: Lossless codec for archiving. Perfect quality, large files.
FFmpegSettings.codec.FLASH: Old Flash Video codec. Rarely used now.
FFmpegSettings.codec.MPEG2: Codec for DVDs and older TV.
FFmpegSettings.codec.MPEG4: Older general-purpose codec. Decent quality, less efficient than H.264.
FFmpegSettings.codec.PNG: Stores every frame as a lossless PNG. High quality, big files.
FFmpegSettings.codec.PRORES: Apple's professional editing codec. High quality, large files.
FFmpegSettings.codec.QTRLE: QuickTime Animation codec. Lossless-ish, good for flat graphics.
FFmpegSettings.codec.THEORA: Free, open codec used with Ogg. Less common today.
FFmpegSettings.video_bitrate: How much video data per second, in kbit/s. Low is a small blurry file; high is large and sharp.
FFmpegSettings.minrate: The lowest bitrate the encoder may use. Mostly for streaming and special needs.
FFmpegSettings.maxrate: The highest bitrate the encoder may use. Limits spikes in busy scenes.
FFmpegSettings.muxrate: Total data rate of the whole file in bits per second. Rarely needs changing.
FFmpegSettings.gopsize: Frames between full 'keyframes'. Low gives easier seeking and bigger files; high gives smaller files.
FFmpegSettings.max_b_frames: Most in-between B-frames allowed. More B-frames shrink the file but make seeking a bit harder.
FFmpegSettings.use_max_b_frames: Lets you set a limit on B-frames instead of letting the encoder decide.
FFmpegSettings.buffersize: Size of the encoder's rate control buffer, in kilobits. Affects how steady the bitrate is.
FFmpegSettings.packetsize: Size of the data packets written into the file, in bytes. Leave default unless required.
FFmpegSettings.constant_rate_factor: Quality target. Better quality means bigger files; lower quality means smaller files.
FFmpegSettings.constant_rate_factor.NONE: Do not use a quality target. Use the Bitrate setting instead.
FFmpegSettings.constant_rate_factor.LOSSLESS: No quality loss at all. Very large files.
FFmpegSettings.constant_rate_factor.PERC_LOSSLESS: Looks identical to lossless to the eye, but smaller.
FFmpegSettings.constant_rate_factor.HIGH: High quality with moderate file size.
FFmpegSettings.constant_rate_factor.CUSTOM: You set the exact quality number yourself.
FFmpegSettings.custom_constant_rate_factor: Your own quality number (CRF). Smaller means better quality and bigger files; larger means smaller files.
FFmpegSettings.ffmpeg_preset: How much time the encoder spends squeezing the video. Slower gives smaller files at the same quality.
FFmpegSettings.ffmpeg_preset.BEST: Slowest encoding, smallest file for the quality.
FFmpegSettings.ffmpeg_preset.GOOD: A balance between speed and file size.
FFmpegSettings.ffmpeg_prores_profile: Which ProRes quality level to use. Higher levels look better and use more space.
FFmpegSettings.ffmpeg_prores_profile.422_PROXY: Smallest ProRes. Good for quick editing copies.
FFmpegSettings.ffmpeg_prores_profile.422_LT: Light version. Smaller files with good quality.
FFmpegSettings.ffmpeg_prores_profile.4444_XQ: Extreme quality for HDR work. Very large files.
FFmpegSettings.use_autosplit: Splits the video into a new file whenever it reaches 2 GB. Helps with old file size limits.
FFmpegSettings.use_lossless_output: Keeps the video with no quality loss. The files become very large.
FFmpegSettings.audio_codec: The method used to compress the audio track.
FFmpegSettings.audio_codec.AAC: Common compressed audio. Good with MP4 files.
FFmpegSettings.audio_codec.AC3: Dolby Digital audio, used for DVDs and home theater.
FFmpegSettings.audio_codec.FLAC: Lossless compressed audio. Perfect quality, larger files.
FFmpegSettings.audio_codec.MP2: Older compressed audio, used in broadcast.
FFmpegSettings.audio_codec.MP3: Very common compressed audio that works nearly everywhere.
FFmpegSettings.audio_codec.OPUS: Modern efficient audio. Excellent quality at low bitrates.
FFmpegSettings.audio_codec.PCM: Uncompressed audio. Perfect quality, large files.
FFmpegSettings.audio_codec.VORBIS: Free compressed audio, used with Ogg and WebM.
FFmpegSettings.audio_bitrate: Audio data per second, in kb/s. Low sounds muffled and small; high sounds clearer.
FFmpegSettings.audio_volume: Overall loudness of the exported audio. 1 is unchanged, below is quieter, above is louder.
FFmpegSettings.audio_mixrate: Samples per second in the audio. 44100 is CD quality, 48000 is standard for video.
FFmpegSettings.audio_channels: How many audio channels the sound has.
FFmpegSettings.audio_channels.MONO: One channel. Same sound from every speaker.
FFmpegSettings.audio_channels.SURROUND51: 5.1 surround: five speakers plus a subwoofer.
FFmpegSettings.audio_channels.SURROUND71: 7.1 surround: seven speakers plus a subwoofer.

ColorManagedViewSettings._: Settings that decide how the raw rendered light is turned into colors you see on screen.
ColorManagedViewSettings.look: An extra artistic color style applied before the final view transform, such as more contrast.
ColorManagedViewSettings.look.NONE: No extra style. Colors are shown as the view transform makes them.
ColorManagedViewSettings.view_transform: The method that turns the render's bright and dark values into what fits on your screen.
ColorManagedViewSettings.view_transform.NONE: No transform is available or selected. Colors are shown without conversion.
ColorManagedViewSettings.exposure: Brightens or darkens the whole image in stops. Each +1 doubles the light; each -1 halves it.
ColorManagedViewSettings.gamma: Changes the mid-tone brightness after everything else. Above 1 darkens mid-tones, below 1 lightens them.
ColorManagedViewSettings.use_curve_mapping: Lets you adjust the image's colors with curve graphs before it is shown.
ColorManagedViewSettings.use_white_balance: Fixes color cast by telling Blender which color should look white.
ColorManagedViewSettings.white_balance_temperature: Sets the color of the light that counts as white. Low is blue-cooler, high is orange-warmer.
ColorManagedViewSettings.white_balance_tint: Shifts the white point between green and magenta. The default of 10 matches daylight.
ColorManagedViewSettings.white_balance_whitepoint: Pick the exact color that should become white. Temperature and Tint update to match.

ColorManagedDisplaySettings._: Settings for the type of screen the colors are prepared for.
ColorManagedDisplaySettings.display_device: The kind of screen the image is prepared for, such as a normal monitor or a wide-color one.
ColorManagedDisplaySettings.display_device.NONE: No display option is listed. The default display is used.
ColorManagedDisplaySettings.emulation: Controls how the chosen display's colors are mapped onto your real screen.
ColorManagedDisplaySettings.emulation.OFF: No emulation. Colors are sent to your screen as they are.
ColorManagedDisplaySettings.emulation.AUTO: Blender decides if emulation is needed based on your screen.

SceneEEVEE._: Settings for EEVEE, Blender's fast render engine: lighting quality, shadows, volumes, blur and speed.
SceneEEVEE.gi_diffuse_bounces: How many times light bounces between light probe grids. 0 turns indirect light off; higher is brighter and slower.
SceneEEVEE.gi_cubemap_resolution: Detail of reflection captures. Higher gives sharper reflections but uses more memory.
SceneEEVEE.gi_cubemap_resolution.4096: Very sharp reflections. Uses the most memory.
SceneEEVEE.gi_visibility_resolution: Detail of the shadow map for each light sample. Higher reduces light leaking but costs memory.
SceneEEVEE.gi_visibility_resolution.8: Lowest detail. May cause light to leak through walls.
SceneEEVEE.gi_visibility_resolution.64: Highest detail. Uses the most memory.
SceneEEVEE.gi_glossy_clamp: Caps how bright glossy reflections can get to reduce sparkly noise. 0 is off; low values can dim highlights.
SceneEEVEE.gi_irradiance_pool_size: Memory set aside for light probe grids. Bigger allows more grids in a scene but uses more memory.
SceneEEVEE.gi_irradiance_pool_size.16: Small pool, very low memory use.
SceneEEVEE.gi_irradiance_pool_size.1024: Largest pool. Uses the most memory.
SceneEEVEE.taa_samples: How many passes the viewport uses to clean up the picture. More is smoother. 0 keeps going without limit.
SceneEEVEE.taa_render_samples: How many passes per pixel in the final render. Low is noisy and fast; high is clean and slower.
SceneEEVEE.use_taa_reprojection: Cleans viewport noise using the previous frames. Smoother, but moving things can leave ghost trails.
SceneEEVEE.ray_tracing_method: How reflections and light are traced. Choose between faster approximations or accurate screen tracing.
SceneEEVEE.ray_tracing_method.PROBE: Uses pre-baked light probes only. Fast but less detailed.
SceneEEVEE.ray_tracing_method.SCREEN: Traces what is visible on screen. More accurate but misses off-screen things.
SceneEEVEE.use_shadow_jitter_viewport: Makes soft shadows more accurate in the viewport. Looks better but slower while editing.
SceneEEVEE.clamp_surface_direct: Caps how bright direct light can be on surfaces to reduce bright speckles. 0 is off; low values dim lights.
SceneEEVEE.clamp_surface_indirect: Caps how bright bounced light can be on surfaces to cut noise. 0 is off; low values dim reflections.
SceneEEVEE.clamp_volume_direct: Caps how bright direct light can be in fog or smoke. 0 is off; low values dim the volume.
SceneEEVEE.clamp_volume_indirect: Caps how bright bounced light can be in fog or smoke. 0 is off; low values dim the volume.
SceneEEVEE.direct_light_intensity: Scales all light coming straight from lights. Above 1 brightens, below 1 dims.
SceneEEVEE.indirect_light_intensity: Scales all bounced light. Above 1 brightens shadows and corners, below 1 darkens them.
SceneEEVEE.volumetric_start: How far from the camera fog and smoke start to be calculated. Higher hides nearby fog.
SceneEEVEE.volumetric_end: How far from the camera fog and smoke stop being calculated. Lower saves quality for nearby fog.
SceneEEVEE.volumetric_tile_size: Detail of fog and smoke. Lower numbers are sharper but use more memory and time.
SceneEEVEE.volumetric_samples: How many steps are used to compute fog. More steps look smoother but use more memory and time.
SceneEEVEE.volumetric_sample_distribution: Puts more steps near the camera. Higher gives sharper nearby fog and coarser far fog.
SceneEEVEE.volumetric_ray_depth: How many surfaces a volume ray can pass through when using accurate intersection. Higher costs more.
SceneEEVEE.volumetric_light_clamp: Caps the brightest light in volumes to remove noise. 0 is off; low values dim light shafts.
SceneEEVEE.use_volumetric_shadows: Lets fog and smoke cast shadows on each other. Looks great but is very slow.
SceneEEVEE.volumetric_shadow_samples: How many samples are used for volume shadows. More is smoother but slower.
SceneEEVEE.use_volume_custom_range: Lets you set your own start and end distance for fog instead of using the camera's.
SceneEEVEE.use_fast_gi: Uses a quicker method for bounced light on rough surfaces. Faster, less exact.
SceneEEVEE.fast_gi_thickness_near: How thick surfaces are assumed to be when computing fast GI. Higher reduces dark halos but can lose detail.
SceneEEVEE.fast_gi_quality: How carefully rays are stepped through the scene. Higher is more accurate and slower.
SceneEEVEE.fast_gi_step_count: How many screen samples each GI ray takes. More steps find more detail but cost time.
SceneEEVEE.fast_gi_ray_count: How many GI rays each pixel sends. More rays mean less noise but slower.
SceneEEVEE.fast_gi_method: Chooses if Fast GI only darkens corners or also adds bounced light.
SceneEEVEE.fast_gi_method.AMBIENT_OCCLUSION_ONLY: Only adds soft darkening in creases and corners. Faster.
SceneEEVEE.fast_gi_method.GLOBAL_ILLUMINATION: Adds darkening and light bouncing between surfaces. Prettier, slower.
SceneEEVEE.fast_gi_distance: Farthest distance other surfaces can affect Fast GI. 0 means no limit. Lower keeps the effect local.
SceneEEVEE.fast_gi_bias: Nudges the surface direction to avoid self-shadow artifacts. Too high loses detail.
SceneEEVEE.fast_gi_resolution: Detail of Fast GI lighting. Lower numbers are sharper but use more memory.
SceneEEVEE.bokeh_max_size: Biggest blur circle allowed for depth of field, in pixels. Lower is faster; higher allows stronger blur.
SceneEEVEE.bokeh_threshold: Brightness above which out-of-focus spots are drawn as blur circles. Lower uses them more, higher is faster.
SceneEEVEE.bokeh_neighbor_max: Ignores very bright blur circles that outshine their neighbors. Lower removes more speckles.
SceneEEVEE.use_bokeh_jittered: Moves the camera slightly each sample for accurate blur in final renders. Needs more samples to look clean.
SceneEEVEE.bokeh_overblur: Adds extra blur to each jittered sample to hide graininess. Too high makes things overly soft.
SceneEEVEE.motion_blur_depth_scale: Controls blur bleeding from background onto foreground. Lower values reduce bleeding.
SceneEEVEE.motion_blur_max: The longest distance a pixel's blur can stretch, in pixels. Higher allows longer streaks.
SceneEEVEE.motion_blur_steps: How many steps the motion blur uses. More steps are smoother but take longer to render.
SceneEEVEE.use_shadows: Lets lights cast shadows. Turn off to render faster, but the scene will look flat.
SceneEEVEE.shadow_pool_size: Memory set aside for shadow maps. Bigger allows more shadows but uses more memory.
SceneEEVEE.shadow_pool_size.2048: Largest pool. Uses the most memory.
SceneEEVEE.shadow_ray_count: How many shadow rays each light sends. More rays give softer, cleaner shadows but slower.
SceneEEVEE.shadow_step_count: How many shadow map samples each shadow ray takes. More steps are more accurate but slower.
SceneEEVEE.light_threshold: Lights dimmer than this are ignored to save time. Higher is faster but may cut faint lights off.
SceneEEVEE.use_overscan: Renders a bit beyond the image edges so screen effects near the border do not vanish.
SceneEEVEE.overscan_size: How much extra area to render around the edges, as a percent. Higher fixes edge glitches but costs time.
SceneEEVEE.use_raytracing: Turns on ray tracing for more accurate reflections and light. Prettier but slower.
SceneEEVEE.shadow_resolution_scale: Scales the detail of all shadow maps. Below 100% is faster and blurrier; above is sharper.

Scene._: The top-level container for your whole project: timeline, frame range, playback, sound and physics.
Scene.use_fake_user: Keeps this scene saved in the file even when nothing is using it.
Scene.use_extra_user: An internal flag marking an extra user of this scene. Mostly for developers.
Scene.is_runtime_data: Marks this scene as temporary. It will not be saved in the .blend file.
Scene.tag: An internal marker that tools use for temporary bookkeeping. You do not need to change it.
Scene.frame_current: The frame you are looking at now on the timeline.
Scene.frame_subframe: The tiny fraction between whole frames at the current time.
Scene.frame_float: The current frame as a decimal number, including the fraction between frames.
Scene.frame_start: The first frame of your animation for playback and rendering.
Scene.frame_end: The last frame of your animation for playback and rendering.
Scene.frame_step: How many frames to skip between rendered frames. 1 renders all; 2 renders every other.
Scene.time_jump_unit: Whether jumping through time moves by frames or by seconds.
Scene.time_jump_delta: How far each time jump moves, in the chosen unit.
Scene.lock_frame_selection_to_range: Stops you from clicking on frames outside the start and end range.
Scene.allow_preroll: Lets playback start a bit before the start frame, so simulations can warm up.
Scene.use_preview_range: Plays only a smaller section of the timeline for quick checks, without changing the render range.
Scene.frame_preview_start: First frame of the preview range used for quick playback.
Scene.frame_preview_end: Last frame of the preview range used for quick playback.
Scene.show_subframe: Allows the current frame to be set to in-between values like 10.5.
Scene.show_keys_from_selected_only: Shows animation channels only for the objects you have selected, to keep lists short.
Scene.use_stamp_note: A note of your own to be added to the render stamp information.
Scene.use_custom_simulation_range: Uses a separate frame range for simulations instead of the scene's range.
Scene.simulation_frame_start: The frame where simulation nodes begin calculating.
Scene.simulation_frame_end: The frame where simulation nodes stop calculating.
Scene.sync_mode: How playback keeps its timing when the computer cannot keep up.
Scene.sync_mode.NONE: Plays every frame, even if it runs slower than real time.
Scene.sync_mode.FRAME_DROP: Skips frames to stay at the right speed.
Scene.sync_mode.AUDIO_SYNC: Skips frames so the picture stays in sync with the sound.
Scene.playback_loop_mode: What happens when playback reaches the end.
Scene.playback_loop_mode.INFINITE: Starts again from the beginning, forever.
Scene.playback_loop_mode.STOP_START_FRAME: Stops and jumps back to the first frame.
Scene.playback_loop_mode.RESTORE: Stops and goes back to the frame where playback began.
Scene.playback_loop_mode.BOUNCE: Plays forward, then backward, again and again.
Scene.use_nodes: Turns on the compositor so you can edit the final image with nodes.
Scene.gravity: The direction and strength of gravity pulling things in physics. Default is 9.81 down.
Scene.use_gravity: Turns gravity on for all physics in the scene. Off means things float.
Scene.use_audio: Plays the sound from the Video Sequencer during playback. Off mutes it.
Scene.use_audio_scrub: Plays sound while you drag the timeline, so you can hear exact moments.
Scene.audio_doppler_speed: How fast sound travels, used for the Doppler effect. Lower makes pitch shift more with motion.
Scene.audio_doppler_factor: How strong the Doppler pitch change is. 0 is off; higher exaggerates the effect.
Scene.audio_distance_model: The rule for how sound gets quieter with distance.
Scene.audio_distance_model.NONE: No change with distance. Sound is equally loud everywhere.
Scene.audio_distance_model.INVERSE: Volume drops quickly at first, then slowly, like real life.
Scene.audio_distance_model.INVERSE_CLAMPED: Like Inverse, but with limits on the closest and farthest volume.
Scene.audio_distance_model.LINEAR: Volume fades out evenly with distance.
Scene.audio_distance_model.LINEAR_CLAMPED: Like Linear, but with limits on the closest and farthest volume.
Scene.audio_distance_model.EXPONENT: Volume drops by a power curve. You can make it fast or slow.
Scene.audio_distance_model.EXPONENT_CLAMPED: Like Exponent, but with limits on the closest and farthest volume.
Scene.audio_volume: The master volume for the scene's sound. 1 is full, 0 is silent.

World._: The world is the environment around your scene: background color, ambient light and the sky's sun.
World.use_fake_user: Keeps this world saved in the file even when no scene is using it.
World.use_extra_user: An internal flag marking an extra user of this world. Mostly for developers.
World.is_runtime_data: Marks this world as temporary. It will not be saved in the .blend file.
World.tag: An internal marker that tools use for temporary bookkeeping. You do not need to change it.
World.use_eevee_finite_volume: Converts old EEVEE Legacy world fog into a form the new EEVEE can render.
World.color: The color of the world background and the ambient light it gives off.
World.use_nodes: Builds the world from shader nodes, which gives full control, such as an HDRI sky.
World.lightgroup: Puts the world's light into a named group so you can adjust it separately in compositing.
World.probe_resolution: Detail of the world lighting stored for reflections. Higher is sharper but uses more memory.
World.probe_resolution.4096: Highest detail, uses the most memory.
World.sun_threshold: Extracts very bright spots in the sky as a real sun light. 0 turns it off; lower values pick up more.
World.sun_angle: The size of the sun in the sky. Small gives sharp shadows; large gives softer shadows.
World.use_sun_shadow: Lets the sun from the world cast shadows.
World.sun_shadow_maximum_resolution: Largest size of a shadow pixel. Higher saves memory but makes shadows blockier.
World.sun_shadow_filter_radius: Blurs shadow edges to hide jagged lines. Higher is softer.
World.use_sun_shadow_jitter: Makes sun shadows smoother and more precise by sampling over time. Slower.
World.sun_shadow_jitter_overblur: Adds blur to each shadow sample to reduce grain. Too high makes shadows soft and vague.

WorldLighting._: Settings for ambient occlusion, which darkens tight corners and creases for more depth.
WorldLighting.ao_factor: How strong the corner darkening is. 0 is none; 1 is full strength.
WorldLighting.distance: How far away surfaces can cause darkening. Small only darkens tight creases; large darkens wider areas.
